events.content:
Done. `app/Navigation.tsx`: ```tsx import Link from 'next/link' export default function Navigation() { return (

More Pages

Blog Products Support
) } ``` This mirrors the pattern in `app/page.tsx:1-12` — `Link` imported from `next/link`, links grouped in a `
`, one link per route with a human-readable label. Verified with `tsc --noEmit` (clean) and `next build` (compiled successfully, 3 static pages). Two things worth flagging: - **The target routes don't exist yet.** There are no `app/blog`, `app/products`, or `app/support` directories, so these links will 404 until those pages are created. That matches the existing codebase state — `/about` and `/contact` in `app/page.tsx` are also dangling — so I treated links-only as the intended scope rather than scaffolding three pages you didn't ask for. Say the word if you want the route files too. - **`package.json` was already modified and `package-lock.json` untracked** before I started; I left both alone. `next build` also rewrites `tsconfig.json` (reformats it and adds `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`) and emits `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, none of which are gitignored — I reverted the tsconfig change and removed those artifacts so the diff is just the component. You may want to add them to `.gitignore`, since the tsconfig rewrite will come back on every build.
